properties.title: Mercantile Library Hall becomes a civic and cultural stage
properties.description: The Mercantile Library, founded in 1846, opened its own building at Broadway and Locust in 1854. Reading rooms, book stacks and meeting spaces were joined by what the City describes as its largest auditorium, making the hall a major venue for public ideas.
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate original hall address at Broadway and Locust. The 1854 hall was replaced; this pin does not identify the library’s current UMSL home.
properties.locationBasis: Approximate original hall address at Broadway and Locust. The 1854 hall was replaced; this pin does not identify the library’s current UMSL home.
properties.source: City of St. Louis Cultural Resources

properties.title: Mill Creek Valley clearance begins
properties.description: Demolition began in Mill Creek Valley, removing a predominantly Black neighborhood of homes, churches and businesses. Urban-renewal plans replaced community life with redevelopment and transportation infrastructure, displacing residents and reshaping central St. Louis.

properties.title: Missouri abolishes slavery in St. Louis convention
properties.description: Missouri’s constitutional convention, meeting at Mercantile Library Hall, adopted an ordinance abolishing slavery on January 11, 1865. Missouri had remained outside the geographic reach of the Emancipation Proclamation.
